steps.say: Tobacco and alcohol multiply each other in the mid oesophagus, which is why the exam pairs them as one synergistic answer. Reflux and obesity produce the other cancer at the other end of the same organ. H. pylori protects distally while harming the stomach, a classic inverse twist. Minor risks remain below the big two for squamous disease.
steps.tx: Mid oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma is driven synergistically by **tobacco smoking** (nitrosamines and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons) with heavy alcohol (acetaldehyde plus mucosal solvent effect), the single strongest combined risk. Obesity, high body mass, reflux and Barrett metaplasia instead drive distal oesophageal and junctional **adenocarcinoma** (gland forming cancer), never squamous cancer. H. pylori predisposes to non cardia gastric cancer while inversely lowering distal adenocarcinoma risk; HPV and prior mediastinal radiation are minor squamous risks.

steps.say: Jelly belly demands the most aggressive abdominal surgery plus heated chemotherapy in one sitting. The mucin source is usually a ruptured appendiceal neoplasm, not a primary peritoneal tumour. True benign myxoma needs excision alone without drugs or radiation. Chemo and radiation resistance characterise the benign lesion.
steps.tx: **Pseudomyxoma peritonei** (jelly belly from diffuse mucinous peritoneal ascites, usually a ruptured low grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm or mucinous ovarian tumour) is cured only by complete cytoreductive surgery with peritonectomy plus hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (**HIPEC** with mitomycin C or oxaliplatin). Benign mesenchymal **myxoma** (hypocellular myxoid tumour) is chemo and radio resistant and needs complete surgical excision alone. Jelly ascites always signals spread, never a primary peritoneal cancer.

steps.say: HER2 three plus opens a tumour blind option after standard lines fail. Breast rules do not travel: low expression counts only in breast cancer. Colon, lung and biliary tumours with strong staining qualify equally. Sequencing for ERBB2 mutation adds lung eligibility beyond staining.
steps.tx: Fam trastuzumab deruxtecan (**T-DXd**, HER2 antibody drug conjugate) holds tumour agnostic approval at second line or later for any unresectable or metastatic solid tumour with **HER2 IHC 3+** (strong complete membrane staining) via DESTINY PanTumor02 and CRC02. **HER2 low** (IHC 1+ or IHC 2+ without amplification) applies exclusively to breast cancer via DESTINY Breast04 and 06, never to non breast tumours which require IHC 3+. ERBB2 mutation qualifies non small cell lung cancer independently of staining.

steps.say: Performance status decides over stage, histology and genetics at the bedside. Three and four indicate the treatment harms faster than the tumour kills. Supportive care maximises comfort without pretending to extend life. Trial and targeted options wait for fitter patients.
steps.tx: Gastric, pancreatic and hepatobiliary carcinomas with **ECOG performance status 3 to 4** (confined to chair or bed over half the day) or Karnofsky below 60 percent receive **best supportive care** (symptom focused palliative care) alone regardless of tumour stage, since active cytotoxic therapy or surgery brings prohibitive toxicity and early mortality. Fitness gates every oncology decision before stage, markers or mutations. Performance status 0 to 2 keeps curative and palliative systemic options open.

steps.say: Location within the anal region decides the histology list completely. True canal cancers are viral driven squamous tumours treated with combined drugs and radiation. Skin outside the verge grows basal cell cancer that never appears inside. Melanoma remains rare in both sites and fares worst.
steps.tx: The true anal canal (anorectal ring to anal verge) develops **squamous cell carcinoma** in 80 to 85 percent (HPV 16 and 18 driven, including basaloid and cloacogenic variants, treated with Nigro chemoradiation of 5 fluorouracil or capecitabine plus mitomycin C with radiation), adenocarcinoma in about 10 percent treated as rectal cancer, and mucosal melanoma in 1 to 3 percent. **Basal cell carcinoma** arises exclusively in hair bearing perianal skin at the anal margin, never inside the true canal, so it is the correct EXCEPT answer.
